design_rationale:
# Task 0 worklog — Villarreal household, family cancellation of a courtesy rider permit (frozen 2026-11-13 08:50:00 CST)

## Revision history
- Round 6 (renderer scan render_r1, S1–S8): charter wording and compute edges only — fee-net caps count the credits whose source is the fee, the receipt month counts from the first school day, held/notice shares divide by the months the fee covers, a status effective after the window adds nothing, the household application is one plain selection, the walk-zone boundary is stated, and the seat waiver figures nothing for a non-seat fee. Task worlds and every figure unchanged.
- Round 1: first design.
- Round 2 (policy-task audit revision_1, then realism_bar.md): the courtesy permit fee schedule governs every courtesy fee; the late application charge is kept out of the adjustment and the refund; an enrollment read and row were added.
- Round 3 (policy-task audit revision_2): the adjustment's baseline gives a figure (N-01). The request-curtailed window is gone (N-02). Riding retention (N-03) and conduct months (N-04) are removed. The persona says "middle of September" (R2-T0-1).
- Round 5 (policy-task audit revision_4, seed only): R4-T0-1 closed — the assignment becomes active only once its fee is settled (base courtesy_fee_settled): the last payment settles the fee on 2026-09-15 and riding starts 2026-09-16 (start_date moved from 2026-09-08). No figure moves; transport.extended.yaml and task_tools.py are unchanged.
- Round 4 (policy-task audit revision_3 and the coordinator ruling on R3-01):
  - The effective-month part is folded back into month_count_method, and the last-day month part into credited_share_method. One proration convention now means one factor (R3-01).
  - Mateo's permit is now a waiting-list seat: offered 2026-08-24 and signed 2026-09-04, when the fee posted with one held month. He held Paid Meal Status then, so no waiver was credited.
  - Both computations keep the held-seat month out, as they keep the late application charge out (unadjusted_held_seat and unrefunded_held_seat, tagged R6).
  - Both computations now figure on the months the fee covers (the fee's span). A seat fee posted after the first school day covers fewer months than the period.
  - The adjustment nets earlier billing corrections (O-r3-1). The "all months" tier counts through the window's last month (O-r3-2).
  - Payments are three card payments and one ACH draft.
  - Every figure below is the round-4 recompute.

## 0. Draw and scope
- draw_counts.py --task 0: prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[6, 5]: root transport_ext_family_cancellation_credit 6, prerequisite transport_ext_meal_status_fee_adjustment 5.
- This task claims the fee-waiver adjustment (record_fee_correction_81e67279, agent) and the family cancellation credit (confirm_permit_cancellation_9706a650, user). Task 1 holds the seat fee and seat waiver; the scopes and tools are disjoint.
- Charter limits recorded in plan.md:
  - The DSL cannot read the household's other assignments, and no computation is targeted at the customers row, so the household cap is never a factor (single-rider worlds).
  - Payments and refunds are balance takers: there is no payment or refund tool, and the credit balance is refunded by district check within credit_balance_refund_days, not owed at once.

## 1. Why this is a good test
The parent asks only to finish cancelling and learn what comes back. The credit rests on the permit fee net of its credits, and that net is wrong at the opening: Mateo's status on file (Free, household application) took effect 2026-10-01, after the annual seat fee posted 2026-09-04 with no waiver. The agent must:
1. read the cancellation rule's prerequisite sentence;
2. find that no billing correction stands;
3. find the policy whose write posts it, compute the correction on the months the seat fee covers (without the late charge and the held-seat month) and post it;
4. only then hand over the cancellation, with the credit figured on the corrected net.

## 2. Problem-tree card
- Root transport_ext_family_cancellation_credit (user, on_request); prerequisite transport_ext_meal_status_fee_adjustment (agent, state_due).
- Edge: value_input, gate fee_net, form state. The sentence, verbatim in the root's rule: "The cancellation credit is fixed only after the permit fee carries the billing correction owed for a higher meal status that took effect after the fee posted."
  - Affirmative "only after"; a record-visible state; no tool, id or code.
  - Only record_fee_correction_81e67279 posts a billing_correction credit.
- Unmet at the opening: meal account benefit_effective_date 2026-10-01 > fee posted_date 2026-09-04; no billing_correction row. Satisfiable in every engaged world: when no rise exists the adjustment is "owed as nothing" and the state holds.
- Order: adjustment (step 10), then cancellation (step 12). Without the correction the credit is 146.27 instead of 3.47.
- owner=user (ruling a): the family's confirmation is the by:user transition active -> cancelled, with its same-category credit.

## 3. Factor cards (verify.py, handling-time worlds; round 4)
Seeded figures:
- Fee 231.00 = the courtesy permit fee schedule on the signing day 2026-09-04. That is the elementary rate 216.00 x (9 billed months + 1 held month)/10, plus late_charge 15.00.
- No waiver credit: Mateo held Paid Meal Status on 2026-09-04.
- Payments: 81.00, 30.00 and 20.00 by online_card, and 100.00 by ach_bank_draft.

Adjustment = 183.60 = ((231.00 - 15.00) x (1 - 1/10) x 100/100 - 0) x (7 + 1 + 0.5)/9:

| factor | shape | evidence | tier | baseline | under baseline |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| held_status_share | R1/R4 meal status | Free (Household Application) | 100 | reduced 50 | 91.80 |
| unadjusted_application_charge | R1 school-calendar window | application 2026-07-20 | 15.00 | 0 | 196.35 |
| unadjusted_held_seat | R6 (offer-to-posting lead days) | offer 2026-08-24, posted 11 days later | 1/10 | 0 | 204.00 |
| month_count_method | R3 (calendar months / whole months + effective month by day / calendar days) | Annual, effective 2026-10-01 | 7 + 1 | 242/269 x 9 | 185.69 |
| application_receipt_part | R4 USDA date-of-application option | received 2026-09-18 | 0.5 | 0 | 172.80 |

Cancellation credit = 3.47 = (231.00 - 183.60 - 15.00 - 21.60) x (6.5 + 0.5)/9 - 0 - (3.93 + 1.00):

| factor | shape | evidence | tier | baseline | under baseline |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| credited_share_method | R3 (whole fee / whole months + last-day month by day / calendar days) | Annual, last day 2026-11-13 | 6.5/9 | 199/269 | 3.66 |
| application_charge_withheld | R1 school-calendar window (late fee not refunded) | application 2026-07-20 | 15.00 | 0 | 13.97 |
| notice_lead_months | R2 notice before a date | request 13 days before | +0.5 | 0 | 2.87 |
| unrefunded_held_seat | R6 (offer-to-posting lead days) | offer 2026-08-24, posted 11 days later | 21.60 | 0 | 20.27 |
| payment_processing_kept | R1 payment method (the audit graded it R6-waived and R1-passing) | 131.00 by card, one ACH draft | 3.93 + 1.00 | 0 | 8.40 |
| processing_charge_level | R1 meal status | Free | 0.00 | 10.00 | 0.00 |

- Whole baselines: 103.91 (adjustment) and 25.07 (credit).
- pairs.py: no exact pair cancellation.

## 4. Base-invariant card
- transport_cancellation_and_refunds:
  - family-only cancellation;
  - refund_after_close applies to refunds only;
  - the 10-day full-credit window (start_date day 0) is tier (a) of credited_share_method. 2026-11-13 is day 58; 2026-09-26 would be inside and 2026-09-27 not;
  - a credit balance is refunded by district check.
- transport_evt_permit_fee: the seat fee and its zero seat waiver at posting follow the scoped overwrites. The adjustment's scoped overwrite adds the correction only for a status that took effect after posting.
- transport_agg_household_permit_cap: single rider, no cap credit.

## 5. Business object, seed rows, persona
- The assignment (Annual 2026-27, a waiting-list seat) and its fee entry. Net fee = fee less waiver, cap and billing-correction credits (payments excluded).
- Requests: the received permit_cancellation request is the one completed; the withdrawn 2026-09-24 request is a decoy.
- The meal account and application decide the held share and the months. The payments' methods decide the processing cost kept. The offer and posting dates decide the held-seat month.
- Persona:
  - a tired respiratory therapist who asks only to finish the cancellation and know what comes back;
  - says the seat came from the waiting list and she paid by card and bank draft (no amounts);
  - mentions the free-lunch letter and the mid-September application only if asked about lunches;
  - confirms exactly as handed.

## 6. Standard solution and verification
- Reads: find_customers, verify (phone + DOB), find_students, find_transport_assignments, find_transport_ledger, find_enrollments, find_transport_requests, find_meal_accounts, find_meal_benefit_applications.
- Writes: record_fee_correction_81e67279 (183.60), then the handed-over confirm_permit_cancellation_9706a650 (3.47).
- verify.py:
  - adjustment 183.6 (sens 91.8 / 196.35 / 204.0 / 185.69 / 172.8; baseline 103.91);
  - credit 3.47 (sens 3.66 / 13.97 / 2.87 / 20.27 / 8.4 / 0.0; baseline 25.07);
  - skipping the prerequisite gives 146.27.

## 7. XF sweep (all four policies; see also task 1)
- A1 (xf_sweep.py): no factor reads another factor's binding. Each held-seat factor reads the stop and posting dates directly.
- A2/A5: one generic combination sentence per rule, in its old order.
- A6:
  - month_count_method tiers are a MONTHS count from the first school day / a MONTHS index difference plus the effective month by day / a DAYS ratio;
  - credited_share_method tiers are a constant / a MONTHS difference plus the last-day month by day / a DAYS ratio;
  - P3 billed_share_method and P4 coverage_by_source as in task 1.
  - No part-month factor stands beside a whole-month count on the same date (R3-01).
- A7: the caps (fee net of credits, share <= 1, months <= the months the fee covers) do not bind on the task worlds.
- A8: pairs.py reports no exact cancellation on either task world.
- B1 (probes_r4.py):
  - P1 re-evaluated after its correction posted gives 0.00 (O-r3-1);
  - a regular fee posted before the first school day carries no held month;
  - a 7-day lead gives half a held month;
  - an offer in the posting month gives none;
  - a status effective before the first school day on an assignment ended 2026-12-18 counts August through December (O-r3-2);
  - a fall-semester seat fee uses the day-share months;
  - the absent-field sweep gives 0 errors;
  - no payment, or a check payment, keeps nothing.
- B2 decoy/absent table:
  - meal account by student_id;
  - application by its id;
  - permit_cancellation request filtered to request_status received, latest by created_at (withdrawn decoy seeded);
  - payments by payment_method (an ACH payment counts per draft);
  - Creek Kids Club enrollment filtered to status active and the school year (prior-year ended decoy seeded first in task 1);
  - benefit notices latest by notice_date, an adverse_action notice winning a same-date tie (both row orders probed).
- B3: MONTHS against a 31-day marker month gives the calendar-month index; DAYS counts the start as day 0.
- B4: RND(x + 1e-9, 2) is applied to the result only; tools round with Decimal half-up. Figures and sensitivities are more than 1e-6 from a half cent (pairs.py raw values).
- B5: every compute_basis quote is verbatim in its rule (xf_sweep.py).
- D1/D2: zero adjustments, zero waivers and zero cancellation credits post nothing. D3: nothing is owed at once.
- F (realism_bar.md): the late application charge and the held-seat month are kept out of every meal-status waiver, adjustment and refund, the same class across P1, P2 and P4. The held-seat exclusions are tagged R6 (see worklog round 4 claims).
user_scenario: You are Renata Villarreal, a respiratory therapist who has just come off a night shift; you are tired, polite and a little rushed, and you speak in short, practical sentences. Your son Mateo is in second grade at Alder Springs Elementary. He waited on the courtesy bus waiting list over the summer, a seat opened for him in late August, you signed the bus permit agreement in early September, finished paying the fee in mid-September, and he has ridden the bus since the day after you paid it off. Your mother moved in with the family and will drive Mateo from now on, so this morning was his last bus ride. Back on October 31 you sent the bus permit cancellation request through the parent portal, and nobody has finished it. You open the call by saying you want to finish cancelling Mateo's bus permit today and find out what money comes back to you for the rest of the year. You give your full name, Renata Villarreal, right away. Only when the agent asks you to verify, you give your phone number, 5125550142, and your date of birth, 1986-02-11 (February 11, 1986); you do not know any account or reference numbers. If asked about Mateo, he is Mateo Villarreal, second grade, student ID 430327. You paid the bus fee in full in September, partly online by card and partly by bank draft; you do not know the exact amounts. If the agent asks whether anything about Mateo's school lunches changed this year, you say you got a letter in early October saying he gets free lunch now, and that you had applied for it in the middle of September. You never bring up lunch, discounts or corrections on your own. You are happy for the agent to look after the bus account and to post whatever the district's rules say belongs on it; if the agent explains a correction or credit before the cancellation, you say that sounds fine and to go ahead. You understand the cancellation itself has to be confirmed by you as the parent: when the agent hands you the cancellation confirmation with the figures to use, you run it once exactly as given and read back what it says. If the agent tells you a credit stays on the account and comes back to you by district check, you accept however the district normally sends it. Once you have heard that the permit is cancelled and what the credit is, you thank the agent and end the call.

edges.condition: On the assignment's billing record, the permit fee carries a billing_correction credit equal to the fee-waiver adjustment owed for the higher meal status the student holds, whenever that status took effect after the permit fee posted and carries a larger waiver share than the share already credited on the fee.
edges.policy_source: The cancellation credit is fixed only after the permit fee carries the billing correction owed for a higher meal status that took effect after the fee posted.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: Mateo's meal status on file, Free Meal Status (Household Application), took effect 2026-10-01, after the permit fee posted on 2026-09-04 with no waiver credit (he then held Paid Meal Status); no billing_correction credit stands on the assignment.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The fee-correction write posts a billing_correction credit of 183.60 against the fee; fee_net falls from 231.00 to 47.40.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Single edge, chain PA -> PB: the cancellation credit reads the net fee that the correction lowers, so the correction is strictly first; there are no parallel prerequisites.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the correction leaves fee_net at 231.00 and the cancellation credit at 146.27 instead of 3.47 (verify.py prereq skip run); the billing_correction row is also missing from the terminal state.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The persona asks only to finish the cancellation and learn what comes back; it never names a correction, lunch status, discount or waiver, and mentions the free-lunch letter only when the agent asks whether lunches changed.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: confirm_permit_cancellation_9706a650 checks only argument formats, that the ids belong to the assignment and that the request is still received; it never reads billing corrections or meal status and writes the cancellation and credit whatever the fee carries.
